```{r}
#| label: setup
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(grid)          # sugarglider::add_glyph_legend() needs grid attached
library(patchwork)
library(sugarglider)
library(cubble)

oz <- ozmaps::abs_ste
world <- map_data("world")

# UT Austin brand: burnt orange, charcoal + secondary blue / limestone / shade
pal <- list(ink = "#333F48", accent = "#BF5700", teal = "#005F86",
            sand = "#F8971F", base = "#ECEAE4", grid = "#9CADB7")

theme_poster <- function(base_size = 14) {
  theme_void(base_size = base_size) +
    theme(plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = NA),
          plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", colour = pal$ink,
                                    margin = margin(b = 6)),
          plot.title.position = "plot",
          legend.position = "bottom")
}
```

```{r}
#| label: header-glyph
# decorative glyph map for the header (referenced by `header-image` above)
p_header <- aus_temp |>
  ggplot(aes(x_major = long, y_major = lat, x_minor = month,
             ymin_minor = tmin, ymax_minor = tmax)) +
  geom_glyph_ribbon(fill = "white", colour = "white", alpha = 0.9) +
  coord_fixed() +
  theme_void()
ggsave("figures/header-glyph.png", p_header, width = 3, height = 3,
       dpi = 300, bg = "transparent")
```


::: {.card accent="blue"}
## [2012]{.yr} From facets to a glyph map

Environmental data often come as **many time series at many locations**,
commonly shown as maps faceted by time. Below, monthly de-seasonalised
surface temperature over Central America for 1997–98.

```{r}
#| label: nasa-prep
nasa_ds <- GGally::nasa |>
  group_by(long, lat) |>
  mutate(diff = residuals(lm(surftemp ~ year + factor(month)))) |>
  ungroup()
lim_x <- range(nasa_ds$long) + c(-1.3, 1.3)
lim_y <- range(nasa_ds$lat) + c(-1.3, 1.3)
w <- 4.4; h <- 3.6                                   # glyph size (degrees)
nasa_ds <- nasa_ds |> filter(year %in% 1997:1998)    # the 24 panels shown
cell <- nasa_ds |> filter(x == 7, y == 9)            # highlighted Pacific cell
cell_box <- function(...) annotate("rect",
  xmin = cell$long[1] - w / 2, xmax = cell$long[1] + w / 2,
  ymin = cell$lat[1] - h / 2, ymax = cell$lat[1] + h / 2, fill = NA, ...)
nasa_thin <- nasa_ds |> filter(x %% 2 == 1, y %% 2 == 1)
r11 <- function(v, rng = range(v)) 2 * (v - rng[1]) / diff(rng) - 1
# simplified land outline (Natural Earth 1:110m, no country borders,
# small islands dropped), shared by the faceted maps and the glyph map
sf::sf_use_s2(FALSE)
land <- rnaturalearth::ne_countries(scale = 110, returnclass = "sf") |>
  sf::st_union() |>
  sf::st_crop(xmin = lim_x[1] - 5, xmax = lim_x[2] + 5,
              ymin = lim_y[1] - 5, ymax = lim_y[2] + 5) |>
  sf::st_cast("POLYGON") |>
  sf::st_as_sf()
land <- land[as.numeric(sf::st_area(land)) > 5e10, ]
countries <- function(colour = "white", ...)
  geom_sf(data = land, colour = colour, inherit.aes = FALSE, ...)
```

```{r}
#| label: nasa-facet
#| fig-width: 5.2
#| fig-height: 4.6
nasa_ds |>
  mutate(panel = factor(format(date, "%b %y"),
                        levels = unique(format(sort(date), "%b %y")))) |>
  ggplot(aes(long, lat, fill = diff)) +
  geom_tile() +
  countries(fill = NA, colour = "grey25", linewidth = 0.3) +   # outline only: tiles cover land too
  cell_box(colour = pal$ink, linewidth = 0.35) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = pal$teal, mid = "white", high = pal$accent,
                       name = "De-seasonalised temperature (K)") +
  facet_wrap(~panel, ncol = 6) +
  coord_sf(xlim = lim_x, ylim = lim_y, expand = FALSE) +
  theme_poster(11) +
  theme(strip.text = element_text(size = 10, colour = pal$ink),
        panel.spacing = unit(1, "pt"),
        plot.margin = margin(0, 0, 0, 0),
        legend.margin = margin(2, 0, 0, 0),
        legend.key.height = unit(0.25, "cm"),
        legend.key.width = unit(1.4, "cm"),
        legend.title.position = "top")
```

::: {.side-by-side}
::: {}
**Trace one location.** Follow the boxed cell through the 24 panels to
get its time series. A **glyph map** draws that series as a small plot at
the cell's location [(Wickham et al., 2012)]{.cite}.
:::
::: {}
```{r}
#| label: nasa-steps
#| fig-width: 2.8
#| fig-height: 1.5
ggplot(cell, aes(as.Date(date), diff)) +
  geom_line(colour = pal$ink, linewidth = 0.4) +
  scale_x_date(date_breaks = "6 months", date_labels = "%b %y") +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = c(0, 5)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "temp. (K)") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 10) +
  theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        panel.border = element_rect(colour = pal$accent, linewidth = 0.8),
        plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = NA))
```
:::
:::

**Do this for every location** to get the full glyph map:

```{r}
#| label: nasa-glyph
#| fig-width: 5.2
#| fig-height: 4.3
ggplot(nasa_thin) +
  countries(fill = pal$base, linewidth = 0.2) +
  cell_box(colour = pal$accent, linewidth = 0.6) +
  geom_glyph(aes(x_major = long, y_major = lat, x_minor = time, y_minor = diff),
             width = w, height = h, colour = pal$ink, linewidth = 0.3) +
  coord_sf(xlim = lim_x, ylim = lim_y, expand = FALSE) +
  theme_poster(12)
```


::: {.takeaway}
<br>

**What the glyph map shows:**

- Equatorial eastern Pacific glyphs share one hump peaking in late 1997
  (the El Niño), fading away from the equator.
- Glyphs over land vary far more month to month than those over the sea.
:::
:::

::: {.colbreak}
:::

::: {.card}
## [2023]{.yr} Four new ggplot2 aesthetics

**cubble** implements the glyph-map transformation in ggplot2 syntax:
`geom_glyph()` takes the major and minor coordinates as four new
**aesthetics**, so making a glyph map is a matter of mapping your
variables onto them. Here: **how long after a storm is it safe to swim
in Sydney?** Share of water samples above the bacteria guideline
(40 enterococci/100 mL) in the 7 days after ≥ 20 mm of rain, 1993–2025
[(TidyTuesday 2025-05-20)]{.cite}.

```{r}
#| label: syd-prep
sf::sf_use_s2(FALSE)
rec <- readr::read_csv("data/sydney-recovery.csv", show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  filter(lat > -33.99, lat < -33.74, long > 151.1) |>
  group_by(swim_site) |> filter(sum(n) >= 80) |> ungroup()
# keep sites whose glyph boxes don't overlap (busiest sites first)
gw <- 0.028; gh <- 0.012                           # glyph size (degrees)
sites <- rec |> group_by(swim_site, region, long, lat) |>
  summarise(n = sum(n), .groups = "drop") |>
  arrange(desc(swim_site == "Tambourine Bay"), desc(n))  # sketch site first
keep <- integer(0)
for (i in seq_len(nrow(sites))) {
  clear <- abs(sites$long[i] - sites$long[keep]) > gw * 0.98 |
           abs(sites$lat[i] - sites$lat[keep]) > gh * 1.05
  if (all(clear)) keep <- c(keep, i)
}
rec <- rec |> filter(swim_site %in% sites$swim_site[keep]) |>
  mutate(water = ifelse(region == "Sydney Harbour", "Harbour", "Ocean beach"))
land <- ozmaps::abs_lga |> sf::st_union() |>       # council boundaries keep the harbour
  sf::st_crop(xmin = 151.0, xmax = 151.4, ymin = -34.1, ymax = -33.65)
xl <- c(151.10, 151.33); yl <- c(-34.0, -33.73)  # glyph map
xs <- c(151.10, 151.31); ys <- c(-33.99, -33.77)  # sketch
site1 <- rec |> filter(swim_site == "Tambourine Bay")
cx <- site1$long[1]; cy <- site1$lat[1]
water_col <- c(Harbour = pal$accent, `Ocean beach` = pal$teal)
```

```{r}
#| label: aes-sketch
#| fig-width: 5.6
#| fig-height: 2.5
role <- function(col) element_text(colour = col, face = "bold", size = 11)
# left: the map, where the spatial coordinates are the *major* axes
p_major <- ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = land, fill = pal$base, colour = NA) +
  annotate("rect", xmin = cx - gw / 2, xmax = cx + gw / 2,
           ymin = cy - gh / 2, ymax = cy + gh / 2,
           fill = NA, colour = pal$ink, linewidth = 0.7) +
  annotate("text", x = cx + gw / 2 + 0.004, y = cy + 0.014, label = "Tambourine\nBay",
           hjust = 0, size = 3, fontface = "bold", colour = pal$ink, lineheight = 0.9) +
  coord_sf(xlim = xs, ylim = ys, expand = FALSE) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(151.15, 151.25)) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = c(-33.95, -33.85)) +
  labs(x = "long  →  x_major", y = "lat  →  y_major") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 10) +
  theme(panel.grid = element_blank(),
        axis.title.x = role(pal$teal), axis.title.y = role(pal$teal),
        axis.text = element_text(colour = pal$teal),
        panel.border = element_rect(colour = pal$teal, linewidth = 0.8),
        plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = NA))
# right: inside one glyph, where the temporal coordinates are the *minor* axes
p_minor <- ggplot(site1, aes(since, unsafe)) +
  geom_line(colour = pal$accent, linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(colour = pal$accent, size = 1.2) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 0:7) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent, limits = c(0, 1)) +
  labs(x = "days since rain  →  x_minor",
       y = "% unsafe  →  y_minor") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 10) +
  theme(panel.grid = element_blank(),
        axis.title.x = role(pal$accent), axis.title.y = role(pal$accent),
        axis.text = element_text(colour = pal$accent),
        panel.border = element_rect(colour = pal$ink, linewidth = 0.8),
        plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = NA),
        # same shape as the glyph box on the map
        aspect.ratio = gh / (gw * cos(cy * pi / 180)))
p_major + p_minor + plot_layout(widths = c(1, 1.5))
```

::: {.caption}
Tambourine Bay's location gives the **major** coordinates; its recovery
curve after rain gives the **minor** coordinates drawn inside its box.
:::

Because the glyph is an ordinary ggplot2 layer, it pieces together with
other layers. The key parts of the code (simplified):

```r
ggplot(beach,
       aes(x_major = long, y_major = lat,
           x_minor = days, y_minor = unsafe,
           colour = water)) +
  geom_sf(data = sydney, inherit.aes = FALSE) + # map
  geom_glyph_box(width = 0.028, height = 0.012) +
  geom_glyph(width = 0.028, height = 0.012) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = ...)
```

```{r}
#| label: cubble-map
#| fig-width: 5.2
#| fig-height: 5.6
ggplot(rec, aes(x_major = long, y_major = lat, x_minor = since, y_minor = unsafe,
                colour = water, group = swim_site)) +
  geom_sf(data = land, fill = pal$base, colour = NA, inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  geom_glyph_box(width = gw, height = gh, colour = pal$grid, fill = "white",
                 alpha = 0.08, linewidth = 0.2) +
  geom_glyph(width = gw, height = gh, linewidth = 0.55, key_glyph = "path") +
  annotate("rect", xmin = cx - gw / 2, xmax = cx + gw / 2,
           ymin = cy - gh / 2, ymax = cy + gh / 2,
           fill = NA, colour = pal$ink, linewidth = 0.9) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = water_col, name = NULL) +
  guides(colour = guide_legend(override.aes = list(linewidth = 1.5))) +
  coord_sf(xlim = xl, ylim = yl, expand = FALSE) +
  theme_poster(14)
```

::: {.takeaway}
- **Ocean beaches** spike the day after a storm (46% of samples
  unsafe), then clear within 2 days (24%).
- **Harbour** sites are worse and slower: 73% unsafe the day after, still
  65% two days later, especially in the inner-harbour coves.
:::
:::

::: {.colbreak}
:::

::: {.card accent="orange"}
## [2026]{.yr} Multivariate glyphs

A line glyph shows **one variable** over time, but many environmental
summaries are **multivariate**: daily minimum *and* maximum, lower *and*
upper quantiles, an estimate *and* its uncertainty. **sugarglider** adds
aesthetics for a second minor variable, transformed the same way:

$$
\begin{aligned}
y_{\min} &= y_{\text{major}} + \frac{h}{2}\,\tilde{y}_{\min,\text{minor}} \\
y_{\max} &= y_{\text{major}} + \frac{h}{2}\,\tilde{y}_{\max,\text{minor}}
\end{aligned}
$$

**Ribbons** fill the band between the two, here with a third variable,
rainfall, as colour and an enlarged legend glyph to read the scale:

```r
aus_temp |>
  ggplot(aes(x_major = long, y_major = lat,
             x_minor = month,
             ymin_minor = tmin,
             ymax_minor = tmax)) +
  add_glyph_boxes() + add_ref_lines() +
  add_glyph_legend() +
  geom_glyph_ribbon(aes(fill = prcp))
```

```{r}
#| label: ribbon-map
#| fig-width: 5.2
#| fig-height: 4.1
set.seed(28493)
aus_temp |>
  mutate(across(c(tmin, tmax), \(x) x / 10)) |>
  group_by(id) |>
  mutate(prcp = mean(prcp, na.rm = TRUE)) |>
  ungroup() |>
  ggplot(aes(x_major = long, y_major = lat, x_minor = month,
             ymin_minor = tmin, ymax_minor = tmax)) +
  geom_sf(data = oz, fill = pal$base, colour = "white", inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  add_glyph_boxes(colour = pal$grid, linewidth = 0.2) +
  sugarglider::add_ref_lines(colour = pal$grid, linewidth = 0.2) +
  add_glyph_legend(fill = pal$teal, colour = pal$teal) +
  geom_glyph_ribbon(aes(fill = prcp, colour = prcp)) +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "#9fdde2", high = "#005F86",
                      aesthetics = c("fill", "colour"),
                      name = "Mean monthly precipitation (mm/10)") +
  coord_sf(xlim = c(112, 155)) +
  theme_poster(14) +
  theme(legend.key.width = unit(1.6, "cm"), legend.title.position = "top")
```

**Segments** draw one bar per time point from the same data:

```r
aus_temp |>
  ggplot(aes(x_major = long, y_major = lat,
             x_minor = month,
             y_minor = tmin, yend_minor = tmax)) +
  add_glyph_boxes() + add_ref_lines() +
  geom_glyph_segment()
```

```{r}
#| label: segment-map
#| fig-width: 5.2
#| fig-height: 3.1
aus_temp |>
  mutate(across(c(tmin, tmax), \(x) x / 10)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x_major = long, y_major = lat, x_minor = month,
             y_minor = tmin, yend_minor = tmax)) +
  geom_sf(data = oz, fill = pal$base, colour = "white", inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  add_glyph_boxes(colour = pal$grid, linewidth = 0.2) +
  sugarglider::add_ref_lines(colour = pal$grid, linewidth = 0.2) +
  geom_glyph_segment(colour = pal$accent, linewidth = 0.35) +
  coord_sf(xlim = c(112, 155)) +
  theme_poster(14)
```

::: {.takeaway}
Wet tropical stations have narrow, flat bands; inland stations show wide
daily ranges and deep winter dips.
:::
:::

::: {.colbreak}
:::

::: {.card}
## Which one should I use?

| | **GGally** | **cubble** | **sugarglider** |
|:--|:--:|:--:|:--:|
| Interface | `glyphs()` → data frame | ggplot2 layer | ggplot2 layer |
| Glyph geometry | line | line | **ribbon, segment** |
| Reference box & line | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| Global / local rescale | via `y_scale` | ✓ | ✓ |
| Polar glyphs | ✓ | ✓ | – |
| Glyph legend & theme | – | – | ✓ |
| Spatio-temporal data structure | – | ✓ | via cubble |
| Interactive (ggiraph, leaflet) | – | via crosstalk | ✓ |
:::

::: {.card accent="blue"}
## Take-home

1. A glyph map shows each site's **temporal shape** and the **spatial pattern** in one plot.
2. If your summary is a **range** (min–max, quantiles, uncertainty), use
   sugarglider's **ribbon** or **segment** glyphs.
3. All three packages work with **ggplot2**, so you can add base maps, colour and
   facets as usual.
:::

::: {.card}
## Get started

```{r}
#| eval: false
#| echo: true
install.packages(
  c("sugarglider", "cubble", "GGally"))
```

```{r}
#| label: qr
#| fig-width: 5.2
#| fig-height: 5.6
qr_plot <- function(url, label) {
  m <- qrcode::qr_code(url) |> unclass()
  df <- expand.grid(y = rev(seq_len(nrow(m))), x = seq_len(ncol(m)))
  df$on <- as.vector(m)
  ggplot(df[df$on, ], aes(x, y)) +
    geom_tile(fill = pal$ink) +
    coord_fixed() +
    labs(title = label) +
    theme_void(base_size = 16) +
    theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold",
                                    colour = pal$ink))
}
qr_plot("https://doi.org/10.32614/RJ-2026-050", "Paper") +
  qr_plot("https://maliny12.github.io/sugarglider/", "sugarglider") +
  qr_plot("https://huizezhang-sherry.github.io/cubble/", "cubble") +
  qr_plot("https://ggobi.github.io/ggally/", "GGally") +
  plot_layout(nrow = 2)
```
